correctness.rationale: The multiplication and all natural bases are reduced exactly to a nonsingular binary dot product and its orthogonal bases. An orthogonal map fixes the canonical ones vector and weight parity; permutations and four-coordinate isometries reduce all noncanonical vectors to weights 1 or 2. This gives both necessity and sufficiency for every asserted graph spectrum and simultaneous-realisation condition in every dimension n>=3. Exhaustive natural-basis computations for n=3,4 and orbit-generator tests through n=9 agree; finite tests are supplemental.

value.rationale: The exact characterization of which graph collections occur across natural bases answers a naturally restricted form of a specific published open problem in every dimension >=3. It distinguishes a canonical, strongly connected orbit from two entire parity-restricted graph spectra, giving a structural and constructive invariant absent from the general normal-form statement.
